tools.name: hallux_check
tools.description:
Does this identifier actually exist, and is it safe? Call before acting on any name you recalled rather than read: a package to install, a module to import, a Docker image, a GitHub Action or repo, a DOI to cite.

Verdicts: exists (proceed, but read `risk`), deprecated (use `successor`), absent (not

tools.name: hallux_check_manifest
tools.description: Call after writing or editing a dependency file and before committing or installing. Checks every dependency in one pass, including dev and optional groups, where an invented name usually arrives. Exact pinned versions are verified too. Supported: package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, Pipf

tools.name: hallux_watch
tools.description: Register identifiers for a signed webhook when their verdict changes: phantom -> squat (someone registered a name models invent) or absent -> exists. Use for a name that came back absent/phantom which the user still intends to use, or a dependency set worth monitoring. Requires an API key; costs 25

tools.name: hallux_report
tools.description: Report identifiers a model produced that turned out not to exist. HALLUX verifies each against its registry and records only absent ones as attestations in the public hallucination ledger, which is how names graduate to `phantom` and get watched for squatting. Requires an API key.

tools.name: hallux_account
tools.description: Show remaining credits for the API key in use (or free-tier status), pricing, and where to buy credits with PayPal.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "hallux_check_command" appears informational but accepts parameters (command) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: hallux_check_command · Private data: hallux_check_manifest, hallux_watch, hallux_report, hallux_account · Public sink: hallux_watch · Destructive: hallux_check_command.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: hallux_check_command · Private data: hallux_check_manifest, hallux_watch, hallux_report, hallux_account · Public sink: hallux_watch · Destructive: hallux_check_command

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
